cover.headline: The masters line, decoded
cover.sub: What owning your masters means, why labels want them, and how to keep yours.

blocks.text: The master is the **recording itself**. Whoever owns it controls licensing, reissues, syncs and the recording side of streaming.
Check your contracts: who owns the masters, and for how long?

left.title: License
left.text: The label rents the recording for a term, then it comes back.

right.title: Sign over
right.text: The label owns the recording, often for good.

blocks.text: If you need a partner, ask for a license with an end date, not a transfer.
When a song lands in an ad, show or game, the **master owner** approves it and collects the master side of the fee.
Keep clean stems and splits on file so you can say yes to a sync fast.
Funding the recording yourself, through a presale or your own savings, is **how you keep the masters**.
Before the next session, decide who pays for it. Whoever pays usually owns it.
